rule: scripts/kstar_inputs.py admits a build script that names a file-system, process or link capability, or has build-dependencies, only through a row here whose `closure` equals the sha256 the rule computes over the script's module closure (each file's path and bytes) and its build-dependencies tables. Each `reads` path is a source input; each `data` path is one too, and every repository path its text names is an input in turn (one level). `outside` names what the script reads that the rule does not hash. A script whose package reads env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR") or env!("OUT_DIR") in an include needs a row too, even when it names no such capability: `rustc_env` lists every key it can print as cargo:rustc-env (an include through a key listed there refuses), and `out_dir` the files it writes into OUT_DIR that an include! may read, each one reviewed to hold no include. A row is a reviewed declaration, not a measurement: when the closure moves, the record is not knowable until someone reads the new closure and updates the row. docs/DECISIONS.md, 2026-11-19, "Q4 source inputs: evaluate an include or refuse", and its corrections of the same day.

crates/clean-cli/build.rs.outside: git: `git -C <manifest dir> ls-files`, `rev-parse` and `cat-file` (build_support/provenance.rs) read the repository metadata under .git and the git configuration, and `head_watch_paths` tests which .git paths exist. The environment variables SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR and CARGO_PKG_VERSION.
